blindSummary:
This is a relatively safe destination for trans visitors. Nothing is criminalised — same-sex activity and gender expression have never been criminalised here — and the government is formally cooperative: it accepted all 12 SOGIESC recommendations at its 2024 UN UPR, including legal gender recognition, and it hosted the UN's independent expert on SOGI in 2023. The capital and the main tourist city have visible trans communities and tourist infrastructure accustomed to diverse visitors.

The risks are street-level and police-level rather than legal: the national human-rights monitoring centre has documented what it called shocking harassment and abuse of transgender women in urban centres, including a reported practice by police in a major tourist city of targeting trans women for extortion and abuse. There is no legal gender recognition yet, no anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, and no hate-crime statute.

For a visitor: low probability of legal trouble; moderate probability of harassment if visibly trans outside tourist areas; police are a risk factor, not a protection, for trans women especially.
blindOutOfScope: The absent legal gender recognition and the discrimination-law gaps are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: Report by the UN's independent expert on SOGI on his January 2023 visit to this country: assesses implementation of standards on violence and discrimination based on SOGI, gives a panoramic view of the situation of LGBT and gender-diverse people here, identifies good practices and challenges, and makes recommendations.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): this country has never criminalised same-sex activity, but the constitution defines marriage as a union between a man and a woman; at its 2024 UN UPR it accepted all 12 LGBTIQ recommendations including seven toward marriage equality; no SOGISC discrimination protections; a 2018 wedding ceremony between two men in a provincial town was interrupted by authorities.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying national-daily article covered a study finding abuses prevalent against this country's transgender women.

National LGBT organisation's page on this country's 4th-cycle UN UPR: all 12 SOGIESC/LGBT+ recommendations officially accepted in 2024 - marriage equality progress, legal gender recognition for self-defined identity, and anti-discrimination measures; includes the civil-society joint submission (Dec 2023) and summary factsheets.

UN development programme's 2014 country report on the situation of LGBT people here: participatory review of the legal and social environment - implicit non-recognition of same-sex marriage under the civil code, varying police interpretations of laws, religious perceptions of sexuality, and cultural attitudes.
Travel guidebook: practical tips for gay and lesbian travellers in this country (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

LGBTQ news outlet (July 2019): a national LGBT organisation's study - 81% of young queer women and trans men here suffer emotional abuse by family; violence includes disownment, beatings, forced marriages and forced rehabilitation purported to fix a person's gender; 35% of under-35s had considered suicide due to family rejection.
blindLocalsOnly: The absent legal gender recognition and the discrimination-law gaps are resident-facing; the reported police extortion practice in the main tourist city primarily affects resident trans women.
